sections.thesis: Treasuries rallied last week as tech fears sent investors into government bonds, giving yields their biggest one-day drop in three years.

sentences.text: Treasuries rallied last week as tech fears sent investors into government bonds, giving yields their biggest one-day drop in three years.
The 10-year yield finished the week at 4.987%, after Friday's oil climb put the focus back on inflation.
The Federal Reserve meets October 27th–28th, and most traders expect it to hold off on raising rates until later meetings.

sections.thesis: Lula won a fourth term as Brazil's president with 51.76 per cent against 48.24 per cent for Flávio Bolsonaro, and investors braced for a negative market reaction.

sentences.text: Lula won a fourth term as Brazil's president with 51.76 per cent against 48.24 per cent for Flávio Bolsonaro, and investors braced for a negative market reaction.
A Brazilian real future contract was down 10 per cent on Sunday evening, and Bolsonaro said he would launch a legal challenge.

sections.thesis: US stocks fell to end a volatile week, caught between doubts over AI spending and inflation fears driven by the Middle East conflict.

sentences.text: US stocks fell to end a volatile week, caught between doubts over AI spending and inflation fears driven by the Middle East conflict.
The S&P 500 ended the week 0.5% lower and the Nasdaq 0.7%, after Meta said it would create a nonvoting share class to raise capital for AI.
Alphabet and Microsoft report on Wednesday and Amazon on Thursday.

sections.thesis: Oil rose on Friday as prospects of escalation in the Middle East raised concerns about supply.

sentences.text: Oil rose on Friday as prospects of escalation in the Middle East raised concerns about supply.
Brent rose 3.1% to $116.72 a barrel, its highest close since April 29, with flows through the Strait of Hormuz still 26% below prewar levels.
In Asian trade on Monday, December Brent fell 1.5% to $115.01 in what was described as a likely technical correction.
